title: Five advantages iPhone 17 Pro will have over the iPhone 17 Air
snippet: Apple’s iPhone 17 event is officially set for September 9. For eager early adopters, the ultra-thin iPhone 17 Air will likely be in consideration alongside iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. Here are five advantages the iPhone 17 Pro will have over the flashy new Air model. more…
fullText:
Apple’s iPhone 17 event is officially set for September 9. For eager early adopters, the ultra-thin iPhone 17 Air will likely be in consideration alongside iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. Here are five advantages the iPhone 17 Pro will have over the flashy new Air model.

Battery life

This should come as no surprise, but it’s an important differentiator nonetheless. iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max are expected to offer significantly better battery life than the ultra-thin iPhone 17 Air.

That would be true even if Apple made no changes to the Pro line this year. But on the Pro Max specifically, the lead will grow wider this year.

Apple is rumored to make the 17 Pro Max even thicker this year to pack a larger battery than ever. There’s no way the 17 Air will even come close to matching that.

Rear camera system

Apple’s Pro models will continue to offer the best rear camera systems. This year, here’s what that means for the iPhone 17 line:

iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max: 48MP Main, Telephoto, and Ultra Wide cameras

iPhone 17 Air: 48MP Main camera

That’s right, Apple’s new Air model will only have a single rear camera.

Anti-reflective display

Apple has been rapidly expanding its use of nano-texture displays that reduce glare in the last couple years. And now the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max are rumored to get their own anti-reflective technology.

This likely won’t be identical to nano-texture, but it should offer similar benefits.

iPhone 17 Air, meanwhile, won’t get an anti-reflective display. It is, however, expected to gain the always-on and 120Hz variable refresh rate features long exclusive to Pro models.

Fully powered A19 Pro chip

Rumors indicate the iPhone 17 Air and Pro models will be surprisingly similar in specs. Both will boast 12GB of RAM, for example, and even include the A19 Pro chip.

If you want the most possible performance, however, the Pro models will have one advantage.

iPhone 17 Air’s A19 Pro chip is rumored to be a binned version with one GPU core disabled. So if you want to get the full GPU count, you’ll need an iPhone 17 Pro or Pro Max.

Wildcard: Reverse wireless charging

Rumors indicate Apple has tested reverse wireless charging in its iPhone 17 Pro models.

The feature is expected to be exclusive to Pro models, and let you charge other Apple devices on the back of your iPhone.

This is the newest iPhone 17 Pro rumor, and there’s reason to be skeptical. But it would certainly be another good way to make use of the extra Pro Max battery gains this year.

title: Seven products Apple will discontinue following iPhone 17 event
snippet: Apple’s iPhone 17 event is officially just around the corner. As new hardware arrives, we can expect Apple to discontinue seven products that it currently sells. more…
fullText:
Apple’s iPhone 17 event is officially just around the corner. As new hardware arrives, we can expect Apple to discontinue seven products that it currently sells.

iPhone 17 is the event headliner. With the arrival of four new iPhones, we can expect Apple to stop selling three iPhones that are currently in its store.

Earlier this year, Apple replaced the antiquated iPhone SE with the more modern iPhone 16e. We currently expect Apple’s entry-priced iPhone to see annual updates, so it’s not going anywhere yet.

However, Apple will likely discontinue the iPhone 15 and iPhone 15 Plus once the iPhone 17 event concludes. Other retailers may still carry these two iPhones, but don’t expect Apple to keep them around in its stores. Assuming this change occurs, each iPhone sold by Apple will support Apple Intelligence for the first time.

Moving up the iPhone line, we can expect to see both the iPhone 16 and iPhone 16 Plus remain in the lineup. Apple typically keeps its two standard flagship models around with a $100 price drop. iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Air will occupy their places in the new lineup.

Then there are the Pro models. Both the iPhone 16 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro Max will no longer be sold by Apple. iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max will take their spots instead. Rather than giving its year-old Pro models a price drop, Apple just stops selling them altogether.

To recap, we should anticipate four iPhones being discontinued on September 9: iPhone 15, iPhone 15 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, and iPhone 16 Pro Max. 

The new iPhone lineup will probably look like this:

iPhone 16e from $599

iPhone 16 from $699

iPhone 16 Plus from $799

iPhone 17 from $799

iPhone 17 Air from $949

iPhone 17 Pro from $1,049

iPhone 17 Pro Max from $1,199

This takes into account iPhone 17 Pro’s rumored $50 price increase for double the storage and iPhone 17 Air’s $50 premium over the original iPhone 16 Plus price. One analyst predicted $1,249 as the iPhone 17 Pro Max price, so that’s on the table as well. Any other changes would be a surprise.

For the remaining three products on their way out next month, we have Apple Watch Series 10, Apple Watch Ultra 2, and possibly AirPods Pro 2.

Apple always replaces its Series model watches, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 replaced the original Ultra watch two years ago. AirPods Pro 2 replaced AirPods Pro, but AirPods 2 and AirPods 3 were sold together until two versions of AirPods 4 arrived. One curve ball could be AirPods Pro 2 hanging around at the same or a lower price if AirPods Pro 3 cost more.

Apple Watch SE (second-gen) is now as old as the first SE was when Apple replaced it, but there’s not much chatter about that for now.

For now, we can reasonably predict that Apple will discontinue four iPhones, two Apple Watch models, and one version of AirPods.

In case you missed it, Apple announced its iPhone 17 event today with the tagline “Awe dropping.” As rumored, the event will take place on September 9. 9to5Mac will be at Apple Park reporting on everything announced around the event.

fullText:
Whenever a new story comes out detailing yet another setback with Apple’s AI initiatives and roadmaps, without fail, someone shows up and asks: “What exactly is Apple behind on?,” or “Catch up? Catch up to what?”.

And while this sort of comment tends to come from people who seem to spend quite a lot of time and effort trying to make sure that everyone knows they don’t care about something, this specific hill they’re choosing to die on is getting increasingly steep. Here’s why.

I will give them this: for the better part of the last two to three years, there was a chasm between the possibilities offered by novel AI techniques and applications, and their practical appeal to everyday users.

That’s no longer the case. Although there’s still plenty of overblown hype around chatbot platforms and, more recently, products like ChatGPT Agent or Claude Artifacts, we increasingly see clear, practical examples of useful AI features being applied directly to places where regular users already spend their time.

Here are just two of them:

COPILOT function in Excel

While this is an experimental feature that Microsoft started rolling out in its Beta Channel, it is still impressive, and it easily conveys a clear productivity gain previously reserved for more advanced users through add-ons, notebooks, and APIs.

With the COPILOT function in Excel, it is now possible to include a prompt right in the formula, and let Copilot do the rest:

To be clear, this is still in the Beta Channel, so feel free to be skeptical until you get to try it for yourself. I certainly am. But even if you don’t deal with spreadsheets, if you can’t see this as something that would be incredibly useful to millions of Numbers users (and how incredibly out of Apple’s reach this looks), I don’t know what to tell you.

Magic Cue

During the recent Made by Google ’90s TV infomercial event, the company showcased a new Android feature that looks like a more advanced and proactive version of exactly what Apple promised two WWDCs ago, and seems further away from delivering now than it did back then.

Here’s Google’s demo:

If you can’t get past the awkwardness of the video, our sister site 9to5Google has a great overview of Magic Cue. Here’s a tidbit:

“If a friend asks you in Google Messages about the address for tonight’s event, Magic Cue will appear at the bottom of the conversation as a Smart Reply-like suggestion with a rainbow outline. A single tap will insert the address from a Gmail confirmation email or Calendar event.“

	

The feature, which will run locally on the device due to a local model, will be exclusive to the Pixel 10 line, which comes out tomorrow. So here’s your easy gripe to hang on to: it’s not out yet.

But if you’ve been following Google’s advances with Gemini, you probably know that this sort of feature tends to be on the list of things Google has actually been delivering on.

Apple, meanwhile, is still not sure about how to get started.

title: Apple is unlikely to announce these products at its September event
snippet: Apple is hosting its biggest event of the year on September 9. New iPhone 17 models, Apple Watch Ultra 3, AirPods Pro 3, and more are expected. But there are a variety of soon-to-release Apple products that likely won’t make a September event appearance. Here’s what not to expect from Apple’s ‘Awe dropping’ event. more…
fullText:
Apple is hosting its biggest event of the year on September 9. New iPhone 17 models, Apple Watch Ultra 3, AirPods Pro 3, and more are expected. But there are a variety of soon-to-release Apple products that likely won’t make a September event appearance. Here’s what not to expect from Apple’s ‘Awe dropping’ event.

New Macs

It’s rare for Macs to make an appearance at Apple’s September event. Most of the time, if the company has new Macs ready, it saves them for October or November releases.

Last year, the M4 MacBook Pro, Mac mini, and iMac debuted at the end of October and shipped early the following month. In 2023, late October brought the M3 MacBook Pro.

But this year, there may not be any new Macs coming for the entire fall.

Apple reportedly has an M5 MacBook Pro nearly ready for launch, but reporting indicates it won’t arrive until early 2026. There’s also a new Mac Pro expected at some point, but launch timing remains unclear.

Even if one of these Macs does make a surprise 2025 appearance, it almost certainly won’t be until October or later.

‘HomePad’ / HomePod Touch

Apple’s home efforts have long felt like a hobby, but the company reportedly has big ambitions to change that.

The long-rumored ‘HomePad’ device (more likely to be called HomePod Touch) is a key part of that. But it’s not expected to launch until 2026.

Bloomberg originally reported that Apple planned a March 2025 release. But delays to Siri’s AI overhaul forced the company to delay the new Home product, and a spring 2026 launch is now expected.

AirPods Max or AirPods 4 successors

Apple often launches new AirPods models at its September event. That’s expected to happen again this year with AirPods Pro 3.

However, rumors indicate there are no revisions coming for the more affordable AirPods 4 or high-end AirPods Max.

AirPods 4 just launched last year, so we shouldn’t expect a major revision until 2026 at the earliest. And despite AirPods Max still lagging behind Apple’s other models in supported features, rumors indicate there’s no new hardware coming any time soon.

Wildcards: M5 iPad Pro, new Apple TV 4K, more

Beyond the iPhone 17 line, new Apple Watch models, and AirPods Pro 3, there are a handful of other products rumored to launch at some point this fall.

It’s unclear, however, whether they’ll debut at Apple’s September event or be saved for release in October or November.

These wildcard products include:

M5 iPad Pro

AirTag 2

Apple TV 4K with A17 Pro

Apple Vision Pro 2

HomePod mini 2

Some of these products could plausibly arrive in the September event. AirTag 2, for example, is typically seen as an iPhone accessory and thus would make a fitting addition.

Between four new iPhones, three new Apple Watch models, and AirPods Pro 3, however, it’s unlikely there will be room for much else.

title: Nomad introduces new Apple Watch Band – Tempo
snippet: I’ve been using Nomad’s Apple Watch bands for years, and I recommend them to anyone with an Apple Watch. They offer a great mix of premium materials, thoughtful design, and durability. That is true of all of their Apple Watch Band categories, from their leather bands to their titanium bands to their best-selling Sports bands. fullText:
I’ve been using Nomad’s Apple Watch bands for years, and I recommend them to anyone with an Apple Watch. They offer a great mix of premium materials, thoughtful design, and durability. That is true of all of their Apple Watch Band categories, from their leather bands to their titanium bands to their best-selling Sports bands. But now, Nomad is introducing a new Apple Watch Band line called the Tempo Band, built with the athlete in mind. This is what you need to know.

The Tempo Band

Nomad has engineered the Tempo Band from the ground up to be used in an athletic setting. It was made to handle sweat and the constant repetition of movement. The Tempo band is molded from high-performance FKM rubber with custom versions to match every Apple size and type. It has a unique curved profile that perfectly matches the lines of the Apple Watch. Here are some specs to take note of:

Made of compression-molded FKM rubber

Pin and tuck system for secure and low-profile fit

Sweat-resistant and fully waterproof

Silver alumnum pin for closure

Has versions for 42mm, 46mm, and 49mm Ultra

The band comes in four colors: black, lumen (highlighter yellow), dusk (purplish), and crush (orange/red). I think my favorite color is the Crush color. But as someone who loves the Nomad Sport band, I was curious how this new Tempo band compares to the current Sport band.

Tempo vs Sport Band

As I mentioned, the Nomad Sport band has been my most-used band type over the last 3 or 4 years. It works great in 99% of settings, is comfortable, and comes in a variety of colors. While the new Tempo band takes some cues from the Sport band, I would say the Tempo band is even more athlete-focused for a few reasons. First, it has a lower profile. It is meant to be worn tightly on your wrist, ensuring the sensors do not break contact with it. It also has a dedicated size for the 42mm, 46mm, and 49mm Ultra Apple Watches. The Sport band only has two sizes. Lastly, the Tempo band is a smoother finish and lines up perfectly with the curvature of the Apple Watch. So I would say that the Tempo band was made for those runners, cyclists, and more serious athletes, but can still be worn in day-to-day settings. 

Pricing, availability, and final thoughts

The new Tempo bands are available today directly from Nomad’s site for $49. They come in three sizes and four colors. I am excited to get my hands on this and take it on a few runs and see how it compares to the Sports band. So stay tuned for a follow-up review on my thoughts! I think this will be a fantastic addition to Nomad’s Apple Watch band lineup.

title: Apple officially announces iPhone 17 event: ‘Awe dropping’
snippet: Apple has officially announced its next product event where it will announce the new iPhone 17 lineup alongside new Apple Watch hardware. The event will take place on Tuesday, September 9. The tagline for the event reads “Awe dropping” and features an infrared view of the Apple logo. more…
fullText:
Apple has officially announced its next product event where it will announce the new iPhone 17 lineup alongside new Apple Watch hardware. The event will take place on Tuesday, September 9. The tagline for the event reads “Awe dropping” and features an infrared view of the Apple logo.

What to expect

Apple will announce four new iPhones, including an ultra thin model.

iPhone 17

iPhone 17 Air

iPhone 17 Pro

iPhone 17 Pro Max

The iPhone 17 is expected to mostly be an internal update to the iPhone 16 design introduced last year. Meanwhile, the iPhone 17 Air will be Apple’s new ultra thin design with a display slightly smaller than the iPhone 16 Plus that it replaces in the lineup. Like the iPhone mini before it, the iPhone Plus is expected to retire after a few short years.

iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max will share similar specs, aside from the display size, and thickness could actually increase this year, especially in the Max size, possibly in service of greater battery life. Both Pro models as well as the Air model should feature a redesigned camera system that spans across the width of the back glass instead of a round box positioned on the top left. Apple is also expected to sell iPhone 17 Pro for a higher price with fewer storage options. We’ll also likely see the iPhone 15, iPhone 16 Pro, and iPhone 16 Pro Max be discontinued following the event.

We also expect to see two updated Apple Watch models:

Apple Watch Series 11

Apple Watch Ultra 3

Apple may also announce AirPods Pro 3 after a few years of revving AirPods Pro 2. At last year’s iPhone event, Apple introduced AirPods 4 and AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancelation, so that hardware is still relatively new.

Meanwhile, Apple may introduce a new premium case option called TechWoven. This technical fabric option is the next successor to leather, following the failed FineWoven fiasco from two years ago.

The name “Liquid Silicone” has been tossed around for Apple’s standard silicone cases. We’ll see if that name sticks or if it was just a rumor.

Both official Apple cases will likely feature lanyard holes on either side of the case bottom. This would support a single lanyard loop like the AirPods Pro 2 case. We may see an official Crossbody Strap accessory that uses both lanyard loop attachments to turn your iPhone into a sling, of sorts.

Separately, a rumored iPhone 4-style Bumper case that wraps around the edges may be planned for the iPhone 17 Air. Apple has also reportedly considered bringing back its discontinued MagSafe battery pack specifically for the iPhone 17 Air at some point.

New Apple Watch models are typically joined by updated watch bands too. This could mean new colors, new designs, and possibly new materials. When Apple dropped leather as part of its Apple 2030 carbon neutrality goal, it replaced existing leather straps with FineWoven versions that are still sold today. Will TechWoven replace FineWoven this year?

	

We’ll see all that and more at Apple’s iPhone 17 event in two weeks.

How to watch

The event will air on Tuesday, September 9, at 10 a.m. PT/1 p.m. ET. The event will be pre-recorded with some media in attendance at Apple Park in Cupertino, California. Apple streams its events on apple.com, YouTube, and the Apple TV app.

As always, 9to5Mac will bring you every detail from the iPhone 17 event as soon as news breaks. Stay tuned to 9to5Mac in the meantime as we continue to learn more about what Apple has planned for its fall event.

Chance Miller and I will be in attendance for 9to5Mac’s hands-on coverage of everything announced in two weeks.

title: Apple still debating Mistral and Perplexity M&A amid looming Google Search shakeup
snippet: Rumors of Apple considering a Perplexity acquisition refuse to cease. Meanwhile, another AI firm continues to be part of the conversation. Both are mentioned in a new report that paints a picture of Eddy Cue as pro-acquisition despite pushback from other Apple executives. more…
fullText:
Rumors of Apple considering a Perplexity acquisition refuse to cease. Meanwhile, another AI firm continues to be part of the conversation. Both are mentioned in a new report that paints a picture of Eddy Cue as pro-acquisition despite pushback from other Apple executives.

A new report from The Information details the latest on Apple’s AI acquisition ambitions. The Information reports that Apple is telling bankers that “it’s carrying on with its strategy of focusing on smaller deals in AI,” despite Tim Cook recently teasing out that Apple is “very open to M&A that accelerates our roadmap.”

Still, both Perplexity and French AI firm Mistral remain part of the conversation within Apple, especially as Apple’s Google Search deal is at the mercy of an upcoming court decision.

The Information cites a “person familiar with his thinking” in reporting that Eddy Cue is most vocal about these sorts of big AI acquisitions. The report claims that Cue previously championed two major M&A deals in the past, specifically Netflix and Tesla, but both were shot down by Tim Cook. 

Another voice inside the company that is less sold on buying its way out of the AI problem is Craig Federighi. According to the report, Federighi is hesitant on any major AI deal because he believes his team can build their way out of Apple’s AI deficit. 

The report goes on to detail how Apple’s acquisition process usually plays out, while noting that the company has a major aversion to overpaying for any company or team. 

Neither Perplexity nor Mistral AI are new to this discussion, and the report doesn’t provide an update on the current thinking behind either acquisition. For its part, Perplexity excels at AI search using models provided by companies like OpenAI and others. Mistral AI is viewed as a smaller player in the space with its own models and expertise at developing new systems.

Beyond this report, Apple has recently been said to be holding a competition of sorts between its in-house AI team and third-party model providers when it comes to building the overhauled Siri. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google are reportedly involved.

Earlier this year, we spotted signs of a Logitech MX Master 4 in the works, replacing the 3S, and we subsequently got a closer look at it. Now a new report says it will include haptic feedback …

The Logitech MX Master 3 and 3S have long been a popular choice for power users, thanks to a combination of ergonomic design, pixel-level precision, customization options, gesture controls, and multi-device pairing. All that has made the device a go-to for many creatives and coders.

A regulatory filing back in May indicated that a new model was on the way, and Logitech accidentally leaked a photo of it the following month. This included a new side button whose purpose is as yet unknown.

German site Winfuture says that the new model will offer haptic feedback.

There are two major innovations in the MX Master 4. The most important is a so-called “Haptic Sense” control panel, which is positioned in the area of the thumb.

A vibration motor integrated there is intended to provide feedback on the specific actions, shortcuts or notifications to the user by means of haptic feedback. The manufacturer states that they want to provide feedback on actions such as a computer change, cursor adjustments or the like. The intensity of the vibrations from the Haptic Sense field can be individualized in the Logi-owned app called Options+.

There’s also a new “actions ring”, located in the thumb rest area, which allows users to set customizable actions in the companion app.

The site says that the MX Master 4 will launch on September 30 for around $150.

title: Hands-on: Kuxiu debuts tiny smart connector charger for iPad: meet the M30 [Updated]
snippet: Kuxiu continues to make some of the best iPad accessories in the game. They were the first to introduce “wireless” charging for the iPad by implementing the smart connector into their products, like the X33 Pro Max. It was the first magnetic iPad stand that also charged your iPad Pro with those smart connectors. They have doubled down on that and made it ultra compact. Today, they unveiled the M30 Magnetic Smart Connector Charger, and I’m so excited about it. Here is what you should know. more…
fullText:
Kuxiu continues to make some of the best iPad accessories in the game. They were the first to introduce “wireless” charging for the iPad by implementing the smart connector into their products, like the X33 Pro Max. It was the first magnetic iPad stand that also charged your iPad Pro with those smart connectors. They have doubled down on that and made it ultra compact. Today, they unveiled the M30 Magnetic Smart Connector Charger, and I’m so excited about it. Here is what you should know. 

Hands-on experience

I have been using Kuxiu’s new M30 iPad charger for a few days now, and the more I use it, the more I wonder: “Why did it take so long for someone to make this?” It just makes sense. Instead of taking up the iPad’s USB-C port, the M30 uses the rear pin connectors to charge, which we’ve known was possible ever since the Magic Keyboard started powering iPads in 2018/2019. Now, it’s finally here in a standalone charger.

The M30 is simple, well-built, has a long braided cable, and does exactly what it promises. On my M4 iPad Pro, it delivers the full 36W charging speed (see image below). Versions are available for every iPad with pin connectors, with charging speeds ranging from 18W to 36W, depending on the model. The magnets are plenty strong, though I wouldn’t recommend relying on the charger alone to hold up the weight of the iPad Pro by dangling it.

The real win here is that it frees up the iPad’s Thunderbolt/USB-C port. Sure, you could use a USB-C hub with passthrough charging, but nothing is faster or more reliable than a direct connection. Combine that practicality with strong build quality and a $39 price point, and the M30 becomes an easy recommendation.

Closer look at the specs

You can see from the images just how small and useful this little charger is. It packs 35W of charging into a charger that is half the size of the traditional MagSafe puck. 

Smart connector charger – no USBC needed

Fast charging support – charges M4 series iPads at 35W and other iPads at 18W

Strong magnetic attachment

2m (6.5ft) braided cable and only 65g in weight

Here is the compatibility list:

Pad Pro 13-inch (M4, 2024)

iPad Pro 11-inch (M4, 2024)

iPad Pro 12.9-inch (3rd / 4th / 5th / 6th Gen)

iPad Pro 11-inch (1st / 2nd / 3rd / 4th Gen)

iPad Air 13-inch (M3 / M2)

iPad Air 11-inch (M3 / M2)

iPad Air 10.9-inch (4th / 5th Gen)

This will NOT be compatible with iPads that don’t include the rear Smart Connector or don’t support Smart Connector charging.

My take

I’m not sure why this has not been thought of before. This is the iPad version of the MagSafe puck. It gives you all the perks of wireless and connected charging in one. This will be great for people who like to use their iPads in bed while still being able to charge their devices. But the actual selling point is that it frees up that USB-C port. In everyday situations, if you want to charge your iPad at full speed, you need to be plugged in, and it takes up that port. So if you also need to plug in a dongle or an HDMI port or anything else, you would not be able to charge your iPad and use that port. The M30 now allows for you to do that. So if you need to charge your iPad while having an SSD plugged in, the M30 allows for that use case. 

I’m excited to get my hands on this soon and will do a follow up review!

fullText:
Since Apple introduced home key, it has quickly become one of the most important features for smart locks. Basic HomeKit support just doesn’t cut it anymore. Unlocking your front door with just a tap from an iPhone or Apple Watch feels magical, and once you’ve experienced it, it’s hard to imagine going back to keys or even an app. Level was one of the first companies to embrace home key, and now it’s back with its most advanced product yet: the Level Lock Pro. It’s the smallest smart lock you can buy, it disappears into your door (doesn’t look like a smart lock at all), and it has Matter over Thread built in.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

What’s included in Level Lock Pro

When you open the box, you get everything you need to replace your existing deadbolt with the Level Lock Pro. Inside is the lock itself, a strike plate, mounting hardware, a CR2 battery, two standard keys, and two NFC key fobs. The fobs work just like home key on your iPhone or Apple Watch. You tap them on the lock and the door opens. I find them useful for kids without iPhones.

The company also sells an optional keypad if you want to use PIN codes for people who need to enter your home on a temporary basis, but it is not required to get started. The battery comes pre installed, so most people can have it running in under fifteen minutes with just a Phillips head screwdriver.

Like previous Level products, it fits standard deadbolt cutouts and aims to disappear inside the doorjamb. If your door has the common bore hole size and backset length, you will be able to install it without extra drilling. For thinner doors, spacers are included so the lock stays secure. All in all, installation for Level Lock Pro is similar to all deadbolts, smart and non smart alike.

Key features

The headline feature of Level Lock Pro is Matter over Thread. That means it connects quickly, stays reliable, and works across all the major platforms including Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Samsung SmartThings. It also supports Bluetooth connections as a backup so the lock keeps working even if the internet or power is out.

The lock is designed to look like a traditional deadbolt. It is 62% smaller than a traditional smart lock and sits completely inside your door. There are no bulky battery packs or external sensors on the frame. One of the most impressive parts is the new door status detection. Instead of relying on a magnetic sticker that can fall off or misalign, Level built the sensor directly into the lock so it knows if the door is open or closed without any extra hardware.

Battery life looks strong from the tech specs, but I have not verified it yet. Level claims that the included CR2 battery lasts up to a year before it needs to be replaced, but your use will cause that to vary. Built in features include auto lock, activity history, guest sharing, and Apple home key support. For unlocking your door, you can use your iPhone and Apple Watch with home key, the Home app, the Level app, NFC fobs, a traditional key, or the keypad.

Level Lock Pro has an IP54 weather rating and an AAA security rating. In practice, IP54 can handle everyday dust, rain, and splashes without issue. It is not designed to survive full submersion in water. If that happens, you probably have bigger problems than a smart lock.

Wrap up

I’ll be doing a full hands on review of Level Lock Pro soon, but based on the specs and my past experience with Level products, this looks to be an incredible smart lock. Level has always focused on combining design, security, and usability in a way that other companies often overlook. With Matter over Thread, built in door status detection, and a form factor that disappears into your door, Level Lock Pro has the potential to be the best option yet for Apple users who want a smart lock that feels natural and reliable.

title: Parallels Desktop 26 arrives with macOS 26 support and enterprise IT management tools
snippet: For nearly two decades, Parallels has been one of the go to solutions for running Windows on the Mac, and with version 26 the company is doubling down on both sides of that equation while making it easier to deploy at work. Parallels Desktop 26 arrives with day one support for macOS 26 Tahoe and Windows 11 25H2, along with a strong set of IT focused improvements that make it easier to manage virtual machines at scale. more…
fullText:
For nearly two decades, Parallels has been one of the go to solutions for running Windows on the Mac, and with version 26 the company is doubling down on both sides of that equation while making it easier to deploy at work. Parallels Desktop 26 arrives with day one support for macOS 26 Tahoe and Windows 11 25H2, along with a strong set of IT focused improvements that make it easier to manage virtual machines at scale.

What is new with Parallels Desktop 26?

For end users, Parallels Desktop 26 is all about making the experience of running virtual machines easier and more reliable. One of the biggest changes is accurate disk visibility inside Windows. In previous versions of Parallels Desktop, Windows would sometimes show incorrect available storage on the Mac. That could lead to freezes or slowdowns during large installations. With Parallels Desktop 26, Windows now sees the actual disk space on the Mac.

Another improvement is support for the new background process restrictions in macOS 26. Apple tightened how apps can run in the background, and Parallels has modified itself so key features like Coherence Mode continue to work without interruption.

“With Parallels Desktop 26, we’re delivering compatibility with Apple’s latest macOS, and powerful new tools for the IT teams and developers who rely on Parallels every day,” said Prashant Ketkar, Chief Technology and Product Officer at Parallels. “This release reflects our ongoing commitment to Apple innovation and our focus on enabling enterprises and IT admins to securely manage and scale their Mac environments.”

What is new for IT teams?

Parallels Desktop 26 also brings a set of features built for IT teams deploying the software across a fleet. One of the most notable is the addition of granular policy controls through the Parallels Desktop Enterprise Management Portal. These controls let IT teams enforce settings like shared folders, USB access, clipboard sharing, and network modes across all virtual machines. That means IT can ensure VMs follow the same security standards as the rest of the organization.

Parallels has renewed a SOC 2 Type II audit, which gives enterprise customers more confidence that the platform meets internal and external security requirements.

Another new resource is a deployment guide that walks teams through how to install and manage a single Windows app on a Mac. With this feature, users get access to the Windows app they need without ever seeing the full Windows or Parallels interface.

IT teams can now also monitor and manage Windows updates inside virtual machines using their device management service. Scripts from Parallels on GitHub allow admins to check update status, run scans, and even trigger installations without needing to touch the virtual machine directly.

Wrap up on Parallels Desktop 26

Parallels Desktop 26 does not include many new end user features outside of support for the latest macOS and Windows versions, but it continues to make the experience better year over year. A key part of this update is the increased visibility and control for IT teams. Between SOC 2 compliance, device management service integration, and granular policy controls, Parallels is positioning itself as a core part of the Apple in the enterprise story when teams need access to Windows apps.

For end users, the improvements around disk space visibility and background process support will make daily use more reliable. Parallels Desktop 26 is available now in Standard, Pro, Business, and Enterprise editions starting at $99 per year for the standard edition.
